title: RAG and Embeddings for Repository Knowledge
subtitle: Advanced · Retrieve evidence before answering

scenes.title: Start with a question the repository can answer
scenes.body: The training index consists of synthetic policy documents.
scenes.code:
Can an order have quantity zero?
Return a source file and revision.
scenes.result: The claim should be checkable in the approved checkout.
scenes.narration: Suppose you ask your agent whether this service accepts zero-quantity orders. A quick answer is useful only if you can find the rule behind it. In this synthetic example, we'll trace one question through retrieval, answer it using a repository passage, then run the same question when the passage is missing. Look for the file and revision in each result.
scenes.focus: Answer from a file and a revision
scenes.action: Start with the exact repository question.

scenes.title: Index small passages with useful metadata
scenes.body: Document fragments carry metadata to retrieval.
scenes.code:
docs/order-policy.md @ 27e4ab1
  Quantity must be a positive integer.
docs/shipping-policy.md @ 27e4ab1
  Delivery dates use the business calendar.
scenes.result: Two synthetic documents, one order-quantity rule.
scenes.narration: Start with two short passages from the approved training checkout. The first says that quantity must be a positive integer. The second explains shipping calendars. Keep the path and commit next to each text fragment. Those fields travel with the retrieved passage so you can still find the original rule when the answer arrives.
scenes.focus: Each passage retains a source path and commit
scenes.action: Inspect the two text passages before indexing.

scenes.title: Represent passages for similarity search
scenes.body: The embedding model supplies vectors for comparison.
scenes.code:
Question → embedding model → query vector
Passages → matching embedding model → vectors
Compare candidates by similarity
scenes.result: Similarity helps locate a passage. Verify the actual text.
scenes.narration: An embedding represents text as a list of numbers. The query and the passages go through the matching embedding model so a retrieval system can compare them. The system uses similarity to rank candidate material. That ranking helps find a likely match. Open the candidate text to decide whether it answers this question, and check the metadata for its revision.
scenes.action: Follow the query and each passage into the same index.

scenes.title: Ask for an answer grounded in the passage
scenes.body: The cited positive-integer rule excludes zero.
scenes.code:
Question: Is zero an allowed order quantity?
Evidence: docs/order-policy.md@27e4ab1
Rule: Quantity must be a positive integer.
Answer with the cited file and revision.
scenes.narration: Now send the question with the selected passage and request a source reference. Retrieval augmented generation, often called R A G, is the pattern you just saw. The system first retrieves relevant evidence, then includes it when generating the response. The answer says zero is invalid and cites the order policy. Open that path at the stated revision and verify the sentence.
scenes.focus: The answer cites the rule that supports it
scenes.action: Generate from the retrieved passage and open its source.

scenes.title: Handle a stale or missing source
scenes.body: An insufficient-evidence response is an observable check.
scenes.code:
Retrieved source: shipping-policy.md
Question: is zero quantity allowed?
Evidence for the rule: missing
scenes.result: The retrieved source has insufficient evidence.
scenes.narration: Now simulate an index gap. The same query gets only the shipping policy. Read it again. There's no rule about order quantity, and the model can say that the retrieved source has insufficient evidence. In an actual repository, a stale index can produce a similar result. Confirm the revision and refresh the approved sources when your process allows it.
scenes.focus: Shipping policy contains no quantity rule
scenes.action: Repeat the query with the supporting passage removed.

scenes.title: Keep retrieval within the approved boundary
scenes.body: Keep source authorization and freshness with the pipeline.
scenes.code:
Approved source → index → authorized retrieval
Evidence: file path, revision, passage
Verification: open the source in the checkout
scenes.result: Both supported-answer and missing-source cases tested.
scenes.narration: Before using the pattern for an actual project, check the allowed source scope and which identities can retrieve documents. Keep the path, revision, and passage visible. Test two cases: an answer supported by a verified rule, and a question whose rule is missing. Those checks let you tell whether the retrieval system is giving the model evidence it can use.
scenes.focus: Check the index's scope and revision
scenes.action: Verify which sources and identities the index serves.
